title: Probing Shared Blind Spots in Ethical Edge Cases Across Major LLMs

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: shared blind spots on ethical edge cases indicate convergence on problematic values despite surface variation in alignment methods. Directly challenges alignment methodology assumptions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires expert ethicists to rate model responses as problematic. Curating 300 contested ethical edge cases requires deep ethics knowledge. CS beginners lack this interdisciplinary expertise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 300 edge cases with expert ratings is substantial. Could be scoped to 50 cases from existing ethics benchmarks, but the expert rating requirement adds sustained coordination effort.

novelty.reasoning: Substantial work exists on LLM moral reasoning comparison. The LLM Ethics Benchmark (2025, Nature Scientific Reports) provides a three-dimensional assessment system. Research shows LLMs emphasize harm/care and fairness while under-representing loyalty, authority, and purity — a shared blind spot. 'Large language models show amplified cognitive biases in moral decision-making' (PMC 2024) documents shared biases. However, the specific framing of shared blind spots on contested ethical edge cases across models — where all models fail similarly — is not yet systematically mapped with expert ethicist ratings. The cross-model convergence angle on contested cases specifically remains partially open.
